blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Too much information is as dangerous as too little. Employees today receive hundreds of emails, messages and notifications every week. When everything is marked urgent, nothing really is.

Good internal communication is not about shouting louder. It is about being clear, timely and human. A short video from the CEO often works better than a long email. A direct message from a line manager often works better than a company-wide announcement.

The biggest mistake is treating internal communication as a one-way channel — leaders talk, employees listen. Real communication is a conversation. It includes listening, answering questions and admitting what is not yet decided.

items.q: According to the text, why is too much information a problem?
options: When everything is urgent, nothing really is
It is more expensive to produce
items.why: "When everything is marked urgent, nothing really is" — o excesso apaga a diferença entre o que importa e o que não importa.

items.q: What does the text say good internal communication is about?
items.why: "It is about being clear, timely and human."

items.q: What does the author call the biggest mistake?
options: Recording videos instead of writing emails
Treating communication as a one-way channel
Letting managers speak for the CEO
items.why: "The biggest mistake is treating internal communication as a one-way channel."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: The more announcements leaders send, the better informed staff are
Admitting what is undecided is part of real communication
A short CEO video can beat a long email
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que volume não é qualidade — mais anúncios não significam gente mais informada.

items.q: The line "Real communication is a conversation" suggests that…
options: Feedback from employees matters as much as the message from leaders
Employees should be free to ignore leaders
items.why: Inferência: conversa implica dois lados — ouvir e responder o funcionário conta tanto quanto falar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver preparando a comunicação de uma nova política. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, before we send anything out, let me walk you through the plan. The new policy goes live next month, and I do not want people finding out about it from a rumour in the corridor.

So here is the sequence. First, I record a short video with the CEO — three minutes, no more. She explains why we are doing this and, honestly, she admits the parts we have not fully worked out yet. People trust that far more than a polished email that pretends everything is decided.

Second, I send each of you a one-page set of talking points. I need every manager saying the same thing to their team, in plain language. If one team hears one story and another team hears something different, we lose them.

Then we hold an all-hands meeting where anyone can ask questions live. That part matters most. If we only broadcast and never listen, this becomes another announcement nobody remembers by Friday. Over-communicate for the first two weeks — I would rather repeat myself than leave a gap for people to fill with worry.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Oliver afraid of if he does not plan the rollout well?
options: People finding out from a rumour in the corridor
The CEO refusing to record the video
items.why: "I do not want people finding out about it from a rumour in the corridor."

items.q: Why does Oliver want the CEO to admit what is not yet decided?
options: Because the policy is not important
Because the video must be longer
Because she has no other information
Because people trust that more than a polished, over-confident message
items.why: "People trust that far more than a polished email that pretends everything is decided."

items.q: Why does Oliver give every manager the same talking points?
options: So managers can skip the meeting
So every team hears a consistent message
items.why: "I need every manager saying the same thing… If one team hears one story and another team hears something different, we lose them."

items.q: What does Oliver mean when he says the all-hands meeting "matters most"?
options: It is the only legal requirement
It is the cheapest part of the plan
Listening and answering questions is more valuable than just broadcasting
items.why: Inferência: para ele, o valor está no diálogo ao vivo — "if we only broadcast and never listen, this becomes another announcement nobody remembers".

items.q: Why does Oliver prefer to over-communicate in the first two weeks?
options: He would rather repeat himself than let people fill a gap with worry
He wants to test the new channels
items.why: "I would rather repeat myself than leave a gap for people to fill with worry."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We will cascade the message through team leaders first." To cascade means to…
options: pass it down level by level through the organisation
items.why: To cascade = desdobrar, passar a informação de cima para baixo, camada por camada.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "At the ___, the whole company gathered to hear the results and ask questions."
items.why: Town hall = reunião geral em que toda a empresa se junta para ouvir e perguntar.

items.q: "Email is the wrong channel for urgent news." A channel is…
options: a means or route used to deliver a message
items.why: Channel = canal, o meio pelo qual a mensagem chega.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Leaders should not just ___; they should also listen and answer."
items.why: Broadcast = transmitir em mão única; o texto contrasta isso com ouvir e responder.

items.q: "During a big change, it is safer to over-communicate." This means to…
options: let managers decide what to say
communicate more often than strictly necessary
items.why: To over-communicate = comunicar em excesso, de propósito, para evitar dúvidas em momentos de mudança.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de comunicação interna. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We will roll out the new policy next month." To roll out means to…
options: introduce or launch it, often in stages
items.why: Roll out = implementar/lançar, muitas vezes de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Please keep everyone in the loop during the change." This means to…
items.why: Keep someone in the loop = manter a pessoa informada, por dentro do assunto.

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on the wording of the message." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The CEO agreed to sign off on the video script." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "A vague email will not get the message across." This means it will not…
items.why: Get the message across = fazer a mensagem ser entendida com clareza.
